strengths: Valuable dataset contribution: 424 hours of curated primate-centric video addressing the gap of human-centric foundation model pretraining

Strong empirical results: Consistent state-of-the-art performance across four diverse primate behavior benchmarks (PanAf500, ChimpACT, BaboonLand, ChimpBehave) with substantial improvements over baselines
Practical and scalable data curation pipeline: Well-motivated multi-stage filtering using CLIP embeddings (82.8% recall, 90.3% precision) and zero-shot primate detection (82.7 mAPₐₗₗ)
Lightweight and efficient model: 220K-parameter frozen classifier outperforms much larger specialized models (e.g., 167M-parameter ChimpVLM) while scaling favorably with limited labels
Comprehensive ablations: Tables 2, 3, and 5 systematically validate dataset components, continual pretraining benefits, and architectural choices
Clear methodology and presentation: Well-structured paper with detailed technical specifications enabling reproducibility
Commitment to resource release: Authors pledge to release majority of dataset and models, benefiting the research community
weaknesses: Evaluation scope does not match dataset diversity: Only evaluates on chimpanzees and baboons despite dataset containing macaques (43%), orangutans, lemurs, and marmosets; no cross-species generalization analysis undermines 'general-purpose' claims

Lack of statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests despite aggregating across 5 classifiers and 3 views; critical for assessing robustness on small datasets (e.g., 2h ChimpACT)

Unexplained continual pretraining anomalies: Table 3 shows counterintuitive accuracy decreases (ChimpACT: −4.72%, PanAf500 B-Acc: −10.9%) that are not analyzed, suggesting potential distribution mismatch or optimization issues

Architectural choices inadequately justified: No comparison of V-JEPA to alternative SSL methods on PriVi data; design decisions (C class tokens, D'=64 projection) appear ad-hoc with minimal ablation effects
Zero-shot detection quality not analyzed: 82.7 mAPₐₗₗ performance could introduce systematic biases; no analysis of failure modes across poses/settings or detection quality variance by dataset source

Reproducibility limitations: 14% of pretraining data cannot be shared; YouTube playlists manually curated (list not provided); relevance classifier trained on only 2,500 images without inter-annotator agreement; training code availability unstated
Missing initialization ablation: Pretraining initialized from VideoMix2M checkpoint; cannot isolate improvements from data vs. architecture vs. initialization
Limited failure analysis: No per-class performance breakdown, no discussion of difficult behavior classes, no error analysis to guide future improvements
Statistical comparison issues: Table 4 has incomplete baseline results; AlphaChimp marked as 'own reproduction' without explanation, complicating direct comparison
Species distribution imbalance: Dataset heavily skewed toward macaques (43%); 5.5% unidentifiable and 3.5% no-primate suggests annotation quality concerns; impact on model learning not discussed
